metrics.why: The change-of-variables sum through the coupling layers gives every unseen row an exact log probability, which is the quantity the flow is trained to raise, here measured on rows it never saw.

metrics.why: With every coupling layer removed the pipeline is the plain base Gaussian, so the gain in held-out log probability over it is what the chain of invertible layers itself contributes.
metrics.baseline: the base Gaussian with the coupling layers removed, scored on the same unseen rows

metrics.why: A flow with enough coupling layers can pile probability onto individual training rows, and because the loss is the same quantity on both spans the gap between them exposes it.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction MSE
notApplicable.why: Every layer is invertible, so mapping a row to the base and back returns the same row and the reconstruction error is zero by construction.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance

notApplicable.why: There is no encoder distribution to compare with a prior, because the base point of a row is a deterministic function of that row through the invertible chain.

notApplicable.why: The base distribution is a Gaussian and not a uniform spread on a sphere, and how well mapped rows match it is already counted inside the likelihood.

asRun.standInNote: The adapter trains a real RealNVP flow with activation normalisation, fixed permutations and affine couplings by exact likelihood, but one conditioned on the outcome and fitted to the current feature row; no row is ever generated and no future path is modelled, so the as-run numbers measure which outcome's flow gives the row the higher exact density, turned into a probability by Bayes' rule.
asRun.probabilityNote: The exact log density of the row is computed through the coupling layers once with the up class embedding and once with the down class embedding, multiplied by one inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows, the log of each class's training share is added, and a softmax over the two outcomes gives the probability of up.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per feature column of the exact negative log density on training rows, against nats per scored bar on validation rows

meaningful.why: The ordering of bars comes only from the gap between the row's exact log density through the couplings with the up embedding and with the down embedding, which the temperature and the prior cannot reorder, so this tests the conditioned flow itself.

Shows what trading the outcome whose class embedding, after the training prior and the temperature, gives the current row the higher density through the couplings would have earned after costs under the engine's rule.
Grades the Bayes posterior from the two coupling-layer densities together with the single validation-fitted temperature, so it tests the flow-plus-temperature pair and not the raw density ratio.
A bounded score of the same posterior, less dominated than the logarithmic loss by bars where the couplings assign the row a vanishing density under one outcome.
A ratio of two exact densities over dozens of feature columns is far too confident, so a slope below one on test bars means the single validation temperature did not shrink it enough.
The prior is the training up share and nothing is class-weighted, so the gap between stated and observed up share tests whether the temperature carried over from validation to test.
A fitted temperature near zero flattens the posterior onto the training prior, and a near-zero spread of the probability of up reveals that the density gap was judged uninformative.

Counts how often the outcome favoured by the two coupling-layer densities after the prior matched the move; the cut depends on the training up share and the fitted temperature as well as on the densities.
Averages the hit rate on up bars and on down bars, which exposes a posterior that follows the training prior and calls one side almost always.
One symmetric number for whether the outcome with the higher coupling-layer density moves with the realised direction across all four cells.
Net profit of the coupling-density direction call per unit of bar-to-bar variation, under the engine's holding rule and costs.
The deepest loss run of trading the coupling-density call, which shows how long the class-conditioned flow stayed on the wrong side.
Winning trade money over losing trade money for the coupling-density call after costs, read beside the trade count because the call flips only when the density gap changes sign.
Share of closed trades of the coupling-density call that ended above zero after costs, which says nothing alone about the size of wins against losses.
Shows whether the density comparison ever leaves the side of the training prior, which decides how to read every trading number.
Tests a second RealNVP flow conditioned on quantile bins of the scaled move, whose forecast is the posterior-weighted average of the bins' training mean moves, against forecasting no change.
The size in points of the miss of that second, bin-conditioned flow's forecast, which can never reach beyond the mean move of its outermost bin.
How often the sign of the bin-weighted forecast from the second flow matched the move, on bars where both are non-zero after rounding to the tick.
The size of the update to the coupling conditioners, where a sudden jump signals the soft-clamped scale terms being driven toward their limit.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training curve holds the exact negative log density per feature column while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the probability of up, so their difference compares different quantities.
Under the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so the share of bars in a position describes the engine's rule and not the flow.

caveats: The kept epoch is the one with the lowest validation negative log density of the true class per feature column, not the lowest validation logarithmic loss that the chart plots, so the marked best epoch need not be the low point of the plotted validation curve; the registry's checkpoint field has no value for this criterion, so it reads none here although an epoch is selected.
The inverse temperature is refitted on the validation rows at every epoch before the validation loss is computed, so the validation curve is in-sample for that one parameter.
Feature rows are standardised with training statistics and clipped at six standard deviations before the density is evaluated, so extreme bars are scored as if they sat at the clip.
The split of columns between the kept half and the moved half of each coupling follows fixed random permutations of the feature columns, which carry no market meaning.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.
For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost per side is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.

neural_ode_generator.summary: A continuous normalizing flow (FFJORD): a neural ODE carries the feature row to a Gaussian, and the integrated Jacobian trace gives its exact density under each outcome.

Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths. The slowest scorer here.

native.produces: An exact probability for a whole image, built by multiplying the probability of each pixel value given all the pixels before it in a fixed reading order, and new images drawn one pixel at a time from those same conditional probabilities.
native.targetVariable: the joint probability of all pixel values of an image, written as a chain of next-pixel probabilities
native.objectiveNote: The likelihood is exact because masked convolutions or a recurrent state let each pixel see only earlier pixels, and it is a likelihood of discrete intensity levels through a softmax per pixel; in the Model Cycle the image architecture is reduced to one dimension, one feature row read column by column.

metrics.why: The chain of next-pixel softmax outputs multiplies into an exact probability for an image the model never saw, so the average logarithm of that probability on unseen images is the quantity it was trained to raise and the score it is ranked by in its own literature.

metrics.why: The summed next-pixel cross-entropy is the same quantity on training and unseen images, so a widening gap between the two shows the masked convolutions or recurrent layers memorising training images instead of learning how pixels depend on their predecessors.
metrics.baseline: a gap of zero

metrics.why: When images are drawn pixel by pixel from the learned conditionals, checking that they sit no closer to training images than unseen real images do confirms the sampler is composing new images rather than reciting stored ones.
metrics.baseline: a ratio of one, where drawn images are no closer to the training images than unseen real images are

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: No critic estimates an earth mover's distance here; an exact-likelihood model is judged by the probability it gives to unseen data, not by a distance between sample clouds.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction MSE
notApplicable.why: Nothing is compressed and rebuilt; each pixel is predicted from the pixels before it, so a reconstruction error never applied to this model.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: The model does not simulate price trajectories or order flow, and its own literature ranks it by exact likelihood rather than by a distance computed in a pretrained embedding.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: The divergence term belongs to a variational autoencoder; this model has no latent code and no prior to regularise toward.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: There is no latent space at all, so there is nothing whose coverage of a sphere could be measured.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction mean squared error
notApplicable.why: The model has no bottleneck and never rebuilds its input; it scores the input directly, so there is no reconstruction error to measure.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler divergence
notApplicable.why: There is no latent variable and no prior; the probability comes straight from the chain of next-pixel predictions, so no divergence term exists.

notApplicable.name: Classifier two-sample test accuracy
notApplicable.why: A judge of samples is the fallback for models with no likelihood, and it is not the headline here because this model's own score is its exact likelihood; sample realism is a separate property that a likelihood does not certify, which is why the nearest-neighbour distance ratio stays as the sample-side diagnostic.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: Natively the model scores and draws images and never takes a position; a trading result exists only after the Model Cycle adds Bayes' rule and a trading rule.

asRun.standInNote: The specification describes a model that scores and draws images pixel by pixel and is judged by the likelihood it gives to unseen images. The runnable adapter cuts each feature column of the current bar into quantile tokens, reads the row as a one-dimensional image in the arbitrary order of the feature columns, so the locality a convolution relies on is arbitrary too, fits the exact likelihood of the tokens once per outcome class with gated causal convolutions or a gated recurrent network, and turns the two likelihoods into a probability of up with Bayes' rule and one validation-fitted temperature. Nothing is sampled and no future path is modelled, so every as-run number measures the class-conditional density of the current row plus that readout.
asRun.probabilityNote: The adapter scores the bar's row of quantile tokens under the up class and under the down class by summing the logarithm of each token's probability given the earlier columns, multiplies the two scores by one inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows, adds the logarithm of the training class shares and takes the softmax, so the probability of up is a tempered Bayes posterior. Bayes' rule and the temperature are applied only after the density is trained and are never minimised during training.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per feature column for the training curve (the negative log-likelihood of the row's tokens under its true class) and nats per bar for the validation curve (the logarithmic loss of the probability of up)

meaningful.why: The ordering of bars comes only from how much more likely the token row is under the up-class chain than under the down-class chain; the fitted temperature cannot reorder bars, so this is the cleanest test of whether the two densities differ in a way that matters.

A ratio of two likelihoods over many feature columns is wildly over-sure before tempering, so the bounded squared miss of the tempered posterior on test bars shows whether one temperature was enough to turn it into usable odds.

It grades the tempered Bayes posterior on test bars, but the single temperature was fitted by maximising this same quantity on the validation rows, so it is read as supporting evidence for the density plus its curve.

The inverse temperature is one number learned on the validation rows; a slope away from one on the test bars means the over-confidence of the token likelihood ratio changed between validation and test and the temperature did not carry over.

The posterior uses the unweighted training class shares as its prior, so stated odds can be compared with the observed up share, keeping in mind that a low fitted temperature squeezes the odds into a couple of bins near the base rate.

When the up-class and down-class token chains are nearly the same the fitted temperature falls toward zero and every bar gets the training class share; the spread of the probability of up shows whether that happened.

It counts how often the tempered posterior falls on the right side of one half, which depends on the training class shares used as the prior, and is read against always calling the fold's training majority class.

Because the prior pulls every call toward the commoner training direction, the mean recall of up bars and down bars shows whether the likelihood ratio of the token rows ever overrides that prior in both directions.
One symmetric number for the hard calls of the tempered posterior, which stays at zero when the class prior decides every bar and the token likelihoods decide none.

The engine goes long when the tempered posterior of up is at least one half and short otherwise, so this is what the density's direction call earned after costs under the engine's rule, read beside buy and hold on the same folds.

Return per unit of bar-to-bar swing of that same direction call; only the side of one half each bar's posterior falls on reaches it, and that side depends on both the token likelihood ratio and the fitted temperature, which sets how strongly the class prior outweighs the ratio, so the size of the probability does not reach it.
The deepest equity fall while trading the posterior's call, which shows the cost of stretches where the token patterns that marked up bars in training stopped marking them.

Winning trade dollars over losing trade dollars for the posterior's direction call; a trade ends when the call flips or the fold ends, so it describes the call's flips rather than each bar's prediction.
Share of closed trades of the posterior's direction call that ended positive after costs, read with the trade count because a posterior held near the class prior rarely flips.

The forecast line comes from a second token density fitted once per price-move quantile bin, whose tempered posterior over bins weights the bins' mean training moves; skill against the no-change forecast tests that second density-plus-readout.

The average miss in points of the bin-weighted forecast, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars because a forecast averaged over bin means can never be larger than the outermost bin's mean move.

How often the sign of the second density's bin-weighted forecast matched the move, counted only where both are non-zero after rounding to the tick; it is a separate fit from the posterior that drives the trades.
The size of the gradient of the token likelihood at each step, before clipping, shows whether the gated convolutions or the recurrent layer trained smoothly; it says nothing about direction.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training curve is the negative log-likelihood of the token row per feature column and the validation curve is the logarithmic loss of the probability of up, so their difference compares unlike quantities.
With the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not anything the density decided.

caveats: The kept epoch is the one with the lowest validation negative log-likelihood of the token row under its true class per feature column, not the lowest validation logarithmic loss; the checkpoint field names the nearest value the registry offers. The inverse temperature is refitted at every epoch on those same validation rows by logarithmic loss before that epoch's validation loss is taken, and once more after the kept epoch is restored, so the validation curve is partly in-sample.
The model's own native score, the log-likelihood of unseen test rows, is not computed by the engine; only the validation value is used, and only to choose the epoch.
The validation rows are in-sample for the temperature, so only the test walk is out of sample for the probability of up.
The registry labels the probability as the model's own, but the adapter code tempers the density ratio with a validation-fitted inverse temperature before Bayes' rule.
The hyperparameter search scores each trial of backbone, hidden size and learning rate by the trading simulator on inner blocks of the training span, not by the likelihood the density is trained on.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so intervals around these numbers need a block bootstrap rather than a simple binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open, and for roots other than MNQ the costs are the MNQ figure applied as a stated assumption.

native.produces: An exact probability for a sequence of tokens, built by multiplying the probability of each token given every token before it, and new sequences written one token at a time from those next-token probabilities.
native.targetVariable: the probability of the next token given all earlier tokens in the sequence, and through their product the probability of the whole sequence
native.objectiveNote: The causal mask on self-attention lets every position look only backward, so the summed next-token cross-entropy is an exact likelihood of the sequence; the literature usually quotes its exponential per token as perplexity, and task fine-tuning afterwards is a separate supervised objective.

metrics.why: The decoder's next-token softmax outputs multiply into an exact probability for a sequence it never saw, so the average logarithm of that probability on unseen sequences is what pre-training raises and what perplexity restates per token.
metrics.baseline: the same held-out log-likelihood when every token is predicted from its training frequency alone, ignoring the earlier tokens

metrics.why: Next-token cross-entropy is the same quantity on training and unseen sequences, so a growing gap shows the attention layers reciting training sequences rather than learning how a token depends on its context.
metrics.baseline: a gap of zero

metrics.why: A large decoder sampled at a low temperature can reproduce passages of its training data word for word, so the closeness of written sequences to training sequences is compared with the closeness of unseen real sequences.
metrics.baseline: a ratio of one, where written sequences are no closer to the training sequences than unseen real sequences are

metrics.why: Each masked attention head spreads its weight over the earlier tokens; the entropy of that spread tells whether a head reads one earlier token or averages the whole context, which explains a prediction but never grades it.

The next-token cross-entropy logged at every step shows whether pre-training is still improving or has flattened, which is a statement about the optimiser's progress and not about the quality of what the decoder writes.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: No critic estimates an earth mover's distance here; a next-token model is judged by the probability it gives to unseen sequences, not by a distance between sample clouds.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction MSE
notApplicable.why: Nothing is compressed and rebuilt; each token is predicted from the tokens before it, so a reconstruction error never applied to this model.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: The model does not simulate price trajectories or order flow, and its own literature ranks it by likelihood and perplexity rather than by a distance in a pretrained embedding.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: The divergence term belongs to a variational autoencoder; a decoder-only transformer has no latent code and no prior to regularise toward.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: There is no latent space sampled from a prior, so there is nothing whose coverage of a sphere could be measured.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction mean squared error
notApplicable.why: The decoder never compresses and rebuilds its input; it predicts each token from the ones before it, so there is no reconstruction error.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler divergence
notApplicable.why: There is no latent variable and no prior; the probability comes straight from the chain of next-token predictions, so no divergence term exists.

notApplicable.name: Classifier two-sample test accuracy
notApplicable.why: A judge of samples is the fallback for models with no likelihood; this model reports an exact likelihood of unseen sequences, which is the stricter test.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: Natively the decoder scores and writes token sequences and never takes a position; a trading result exists only after the Model Cycle adds Bayes' rule and a trading rule.

asRun.standInNote: The specification describes a decoder that is pre-trained on long text sequences and writes new text token by token. The runnable adapter cuts each feature column of the current bar into quantile tokens, so the tokens are feature columns in an arbitrary order rather than words and one bar is one short sequence, puts an outcome token in front, trains a causal-mask transformer from scratch on next-token cross-entropy, and turns the likelihood of the row under each outcome into a probability of up with Bayes' rule and one validation-fitted temperature. Nothing is written or sampled and no future path is modelled, so every as-run number measures the class-conditional density of the current row plus that readout.
asRun.probabilityNote: The adapter runs the causal-mask transformer twice on the bar's row of quantile tokens, once with the up outcome token in front and once with the down one, sums the logarithm of each next-token probability, multiplies the two sums by one inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows, adds the logarithm of the training class shares and takes the softmax, so the probability of up is a tempered Bayes posterior. Bayes' rule and the temperature are applied only after the transformer is trained and are never minimised during training.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per feature column for the training curve (the next-token cross-entropy of the row under its true outcome token) and nats per bar for the validation curve (the logarithmic loss of the probability of up)

meaningful.why: The ordering of bars comes only from how much more likely the token row is when the transformer is prompted with the up outcome token than with the down one; the fitted temperature cannot reorder bars, so this is the cleanest test of whether the outcome token changes the predicted tokens in a way that matters.

A ratio of two sequence likelihoods summed over many feature columns is wildly over-sure before tempering, so the bounded squared miss of the tempered posterior on test bars shows whether one temperature was enough to turn it into usable odds.

It grades the tempered Bayes posterior on test bars, but the single temperature was fitted by maximising this same quantity on the validation rows, so it is read as supporting evidence for the transformer density plus its curve.

The inverse temperature is one number learned on the validation rows; a slope away from one on the test bars means the over-confidence of the next-token likelihood ratio changed between validation and test and the temperature did not carry over.

The posterior uses the unweighted training class shares as its prior, so stated odds can be compared with the observed up share, keeping in mind that a low fitted temperature squeezes the odds into a couple of bins near the base rate.

When the transformer predicts the same tokens whichever outcome token it is prompted with, the fitted temperature falls toward zero and every bar gets the training class share; the spread of the probability of up shows whether that happened.

It counts how often the tempered posterior falls on the right side of one half, which depends on the training class shares used as the prior, and is read against always calling the fold's training majority class.

Because the prior pulls every call toward the commoner training direction, the mean recall of up bars and down bars shows whether the outcome-prompted likelihood ratio ever overrides that prior in both directions.
One symmetric number for the hard calls of the tempered posterior, which stays at zero when the class prior decides every bar and the next-token likelihoods decide none.

The engine goes long when the tempered posterior of up is at least one half and short otherwise, so this is what the transformer density's direction call earned after costs under the engine's rule, read beside buy and hold on the same folds.

Return per unit of bar-to-bar swing of that same direction call; only the side of one half each bar's posterior falls on reaches it, and that side depends on both the next-token likelihood ratio and the fitted temperature, which sets how strongly the class prior outweighs the ratio, so the size of the probability does not reach it.
The deepest equity fall while trading the posterior's call, which shows the cost of stretches where the token sequences that followed the up outcome token in training stopped appearing before rises.

Winning trade dollars over losing trade dollars for the posterior's direction call; a trade ends when the call flips or the fold ends, so it describes the call's flips rather than each bar's prediction.
Share of closed trades of the posterior's direction call that ended positive after costs, read with the trade count because a posterior held near the class prior rarely flips.

The forecast line comes from a second transformer whose leading token names a price-move quantile bin, and whose tempered posterior over bins weights the bins' mean training moves; skill against the no-change forecast tests that second density-plus-readout.

The average miss in points of the bin-weighted forecast, read beside the no-change forecast's miss on the same bars because a forecast averaged over bin means can never be larger than the outermost bin's mean move.

How often the sign of the second transformer's bin-weighted forecast matched the move, counted only where both are non-zero after rounding to the tick; it is a separate fit from the posterior that drives the trades.
The size of the gradient of the next-token cross-entropy at each step, before clipping, shows whether the attention layers trained smoothly; it says nothing about direction.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training curve is the next-token cross-entropy of the row per feature column and the validation curve is the logarithmic loss of the probability of up, so their difference compares unlike quantities.
With the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so exposure describes the engine's rule and not anything the transformer decided.

caveats: The kept epoch is the one with the lowest validation next-token negative log-likelihood of the row under its true outcome token per feature column, not the lowest validation logarithmic loss; the checkpoint field names the nearest value the registry offers. The inverse temperature is refitted at every epoch on those same validation rows by logarithmic loss before that epoch's validation loss is taken, and once more after the kept epoch is restored, so the validation curve is partly in-sample.
The model's own native score, the log-likelihood of unseen test rows, is not computed by the engine; only the validation value is used, and only to choose the epoch.
The validation rows are in-sample for the temperature, so only the test walk is out of sample for the probability of up.
The registry labels the probability as the model's own, but the adapter code tempers the density ratio with a validation-fitted inverse temperature before Bayes' rule.
The attention weights of the decoder are not exported, so the attention entropy named in the native record cannot be read from a run.
The hyperparameter search scores each trial of hidden size and learning rate by the trading simulator on inner blocks of the training span, not by the likelihood the transformer is trained on.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so intervals around these numbers need a block bootstrap rather than a simple binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open, and for roots other than MNQ the costs are the MNQ figure applied as a stated assumption.

diffusion_model.summary: A class-conditional DDPM learns to remove noise from the bar's feature row; the outcome whose model denoises the row best is the likely one (the diffusion classifier).
diffusion_model.implementationNote: Bridge: diffusion classifier - score_k is minus the mean epsilon-prediction error of the outcome-k DDPM (cosine schedule) on one fixed grid of (step, noise) draws; Bayes' rule, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: nothing is sampled. Expect: class-conditional density of the current row plus Bayes' rule, not future paths; the denoising error is an ELBO surrogate calibrated on validation.

native.produces: A network that, given a sample blurred by a known amount of Gaussian noise and the step of the noising schedule, predicts the noise that was added, so that new samples can be drawn by starting from pure noise and removing the predicted noise step by step.
native.targetVariable: the Gaussian noise vector that was mixed into a clean data sample at a randomly drawn step of the fixed variance schedule
native.objectiveNote: The denoising diffusion probabilistic model trains on the equally weighted squared noise-prediction error, a simplification of the variational bound on the negative log-likelihood, so the loss ranks fits of the same schedule but is not itself a likelihood.

metrics.why: The network is trained only to guess the noise mixed into a sample at each schedule step, so the same guess scored on samples it never trained on, step by step, shows whether it learned the shape of the data or memorised the training samples; early steps test fine detail and late steps test the broad shape.
metrics.baseline: the same held-out samples scored by a denoiser that predicts zero noise at every step

metrics.why: After the reverse chain has walked from pure noise back to a sample, this asks how many of those finished samples land inside the cloud of real samples, which the per-step noise error cannot show because small step errors compound along the chain.
metrics.baseline: held-out real samples scored against the same real neighbourhoods

metrics.why: The specification claims the reverse chain avoids mode collapse; this checks the claim by asking how many kinds of real sample have at least one finished chain sample nearby.
metrics.baseline: held-out real samples scored against the training samples' neighbourhoods

metrics.why: A denoiser with enough capacity can learn to steer every reverse chain onto a stored training sample, which would pass fidelity and coverage checks, so the distance from each drawn sample to its closest training sample is compared with the same distance for real unseen samples.
metrics.baseline: the distance from held-out real samples to their nearest training sample

metrics.why: A fresh judge trained after the denoiser is frozen tries to tell samples produced by the reverse chain from real validation samples; a judge that can do no better than a coin flip means the chain's output is indistinguishable on the features that judge reads.
metrics.baseline: a judge that guesses at random between real and drawn samples

metrics.why: When the diffusion model is used to draw market return series, the drawn series should show the fat tails and volatility clustering of the real tape, and the distance between the drawn and real return distributions is the honest version of the old distribution-distance row.
metrics.baseline: the same distances between two disjoint stretches of the real series

metrics.why: The squared noise-prediction error per epoch only shows that the optimiser has settled; because each batch draws new schedule steps and new noise the curve is noisy and its level says nothing about how good the finished samples are.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction MSE
notApplicable.why: A diffusion model has no bottleneck that rebuilds its input; its trained error is the noise-prediction error, which the held-out denoising error by noise level reports.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: No agreed pretrained feature network for market data exists to define it, and the registry measures the same question with precision and recall of drawn samples.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: The forward noising process is fixed and has no learned posterior, so there is no divergence term between a code and a prior to report.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: It belongs to contrastive embeddings; the only latent here is the scheduled Gaussian noise, which is not learned.

notApplicable.name: Held-out log-likelihood
notApplicable.why: The equally weighted noise-prediction loss is not the variational bound, so no likelihood comes out of this training; any figure would be an estimate from a separately weighted bound and would have to say so.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction mean squared error
notApplicable.why: Nothing is squeezed through a narrow code and rebuilt; the forward process only adds noise, and the error the model is trained on is the noise-prediction error reported per noise level.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet market distance
notApplicable.why: The Fréchet distance needs an agreed pretrained feature network, which exists for photographs and not for market rows, so fidelity and coverage of drawn samples are measured separately by precision and recall.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler divergence
notApplicable.why: There is no learned encoder whose code is pulled toward a prior; the noised versions of a sample are produced by a fixed schedule with nothing to fit.

notApplicable.name: Latent uniformity
notApplicable.why: Uniformity describes an embedding learned by a contrastive model; the end state of the noising schedule is Gaussian noise by construction, so there is no learned embedding to spread out.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A sample generator takes no position; a trading result exists only after the Model Cycle adds Bayes' rule and its trading rule, which is the as-run layer.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter never draws a sample: it trains one denoiser, told whether the bar went up or down, to predict the noise added to the bar's current standardised feature row on a cosine schedule, then calls the outcome whose conditioning denoises the row better the likelier one and turns that into a probability with Bayes' rule and one temperature fitted on validation rows. The as-run numbers therefore measure a class-conditional model of the current feature row plus that readout, not generated future paths.
asRun.probabilityNote: For each bar the adapter averages the squared noise-prediction error of the up-conditioned and of the down-conditioned denoiser over one fixed grid of schedule steps and noise vectors, takes minus those errors as class scores, multiplies them by a single inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows, adds the logarithm of the training class shares and applies a softmax.

stepQuantity.unit: training rows: squared noise-prediction error per feature column; validation rows: nats

meaningful.why: On the test walk this grades the whole chain as it is used: the gap between the up-conditioned and down-conditioned noise-prediction errors, stretched by the one validation-fitted temperature and shifted by the training class shares; it is unweighted, so it is read against quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.

The fitted temperature cannot be negative and the class-share shift is the same for every bar, so the ordering of bars comes from the raw gap between the two conditioned denoising errors alone; this is the cleanest test of whether the perceptron denoiser learned anything that separates up rows from down rows.

A bounded second opinion on the same Bayes posterior, less dominated than the logarithmic loss by the few bars where a large denoising-error gap and the temperature push the probability close to certainty.

The denoising error has no natural scale, so the stated odds are only as good as the one temperature fitted on validation rows; this shows whether that single number still fits on test bars, and because the fit is not class weighted the comparison with the observed up share is fair.

A slope away from one on test bars says the temperature that suited the validation span stretches the denoising-error gap too much or too little later, without the binning that hides this when probabilities crowd near one half.
When the two conditioned denoisers make nearly the same error the fitted temperature shrinks toward zero and every bar gets the training up share; a spread near zero here reveals that collapse.

The hard call is up when the tempered denoising-error gap plus the logarithm of the training class-share ratio is not negative, so the hit rate tests the gap, the temperature and the training prior together and is read beside the majority-class accuracy.

Because the training class shares enter the call, a weak denoising-error gap lets the prior decide and the model calls one side almost always; averaging the hit rate over up bars and down bars exposes that.
One symmetric number for the hard calls of the Bayes posterior that stays at zero when the prior term makes the model call a single side on every bar.
Shows how often the denoising-error gap overrode the training class shares; a value at zero or one means the prior made every call and every trading number describes a constant position.

What the direction calls of the diffusion classifier earned under the engine's rule after costs; only the sign of the posterior against one half reaches this number, never the size of the denoising-error gap.

Return per unit of bar-to-bar swing of the same calls under the engine's rule; it tests the sign of the tempered denoising-error gap plus prior and is read beside the predicted up share and the trade count.
The deepest fall of the equity curve produced by following the diffusion classifier's calls; it describes the path of the engine's rule applied to those calls.
Winning over losing trade totals of the same calls after costs; a trade here is a run of bars over which the posterior stayed on one side of one half.
Share of those runs that ended with a net gain; it depends on how often the denoising-error gap flips the call and so is read with the trade count.

How many trades the diffusion classifier's calls closed; when the training class shares decide every call the count is only the stops, targets and fold ends, so a profit built on so few trades is the drift of one held position and not evidence that the gap between the two conditioned noise-prediction errors carried information.

The net profit of the diffusion classifier's calls minus what holding a long position through the same folds earned; when the fitted inverse temperature is near zero the training prior decides every call and the result is the fold's drift, so only a gain over this reference can be credited to the denoiser.

The mean size, before clipping, of the gradient of the perceptron denoiser's noise-prediction loss over each epoch's batches; it shows whether training ran smoothly or exploded or stalled and says nothing about whether the up-conditioned and down-conditioned denoisers differ.

The forecast line comes from a second diffusion model of the same kind fitted separately: its denoiser is conditioned on which training-quantile bin of the scaled move followed the row, and the forecast is the posterior-weighted mean of the bins' training moves; this tests that second model against forecasting no move.
The size in points of the miss of that second, bin-conditioned diffusion model's posterior-weighted mean move, read beside the error of forecasting no move on the same bars.
Whether the sign of the bin-conditioned model's mean move matched the actual move; it is a different fitted model from the two-class one that makes the traded call, so the two can disagree.

The search over the denoiser's size and learning rate is scored by the engine's shared tuning objective on inner blocks of the training span, not by the denoising error, and the best trial's score is optimistic by construction.
The training curve is the class-conditional noise-prediction error per feature column and shows only that the denoiser converged; the validation curve beside it is a different quantity.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training curve holds the noise-prediction error and the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the final probability, so their difference compares two different quantities.
The fit is not class weighted and the posterior carries the training class shares, so a score that gives each class half the weight grades the model against a prior it does not use.
With long_only off and no stop or target the engine is never flat once the first call is made, so the exposure describes the engine's rule and not the diffusion classifier.

caveats: The kept epoch is the one with the lowest validation noise-prediction error of the true class per feature column, not the lowest validation logarithmic loss; no registry checkpoint value names that quantity, so the checkpoint field records none and the plotted validation logarithmic loss did not pick the epoch.
The inverse temperature and the kept epoch are both chosen on the validation rows, so the validation loss is partly in-sample and only the test walk is out of sample.

Each bar is scored on one fixed grid of scoring_noise_draws schedule steps and noise vectors drawn once from the seed, so the score is repeatable but a different seed gives a different score for the same bar.
If the fitted inverse temperature is near zero every bar receives the training up share, the call is the training majority side throughout and the trading numbers describe a constant position.
The position follows the sign of the latest call and a same-direction call is kept with no new trade, so the trade count counts call flips, stops, targets and fold ends.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks label_horizon_bars ahead, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance, never a binomial interval.
For any root other than MNQ the cost charged is the MNQ account figure, a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

unet_diffusion.summary: The diffusion classifier with a one-dimensional U-Net denoiser: the row is a signal that is encoded, attended at the bottleneck and decoded with skip connections.
unet_diffusion.implementationNote: Bridge: diffusion classifier with a 1-D U-Net denoiser (residual blocks, bottleneck attention, skips), fixed noise grid, Bayes' rule, validation temperature. Expect: class-conditional density of the current row plus Bayes' rule, not future paths; the denoising error is an ELBO surrogate calibrated on validation.

native.produces: A denoising network for a diffusion sampler: an encoder that shrinks the noisy input, a bottleneck with self-attention, and a decoder that grows it back while copying detail across skip connections, returning a noise or score estimate the same shape as the input.
native.targetVariable: the Gaussian noise that was mixed into a clean sample at a schedule step, predicted at every position of the input
native.objectiveNote: The U-Net has no objective of its own; it is the backbone that carries the host diffusion model's noise-prediction loss, and its contribution is the skip connections and bottleneck attention that let one network handle every noise level.

metrics.why: The skip connections are there to carry fine detail around the bottleneck and the bottleneck attention to carry the overall shape, so the noise-prediction error on unseen samples split by schedule step shows whether the backbone really serves both the lightly blurred and the heavily blurred ends.
metrics.baseline: the same held-out samples scored by a denoiser that predicts zero noise at every step

metrics.why: A backbone earns its place only against the same diffusion model with the backbone simplified, so the held-out denoising error is compared with the same sampler whose skip connections are removed or whose denoiser is a plain stack of dense layers.
metrics.baseline: the same diffusion sampler with a plain dense-layer denoiser

metrics.why: The decoder's copied detail is supposed to make finished samples sharp and realistic, and this counts how many samples drawn through the reverse chain with this backbone fall inside the cloud of real samples.
metrics.baseline: held-out real samples scored against the same real neighbourhoods

metrics.why: A backbone with enough capacity to sharpen samples can still serve only some kinds of them, so the share of real samples with a drawn sample nearby is read beside fidelity.
metrics.baseline: held-out real samples scored against the training samples' neighbourhoods

metrics.why: When the host sampler draws market return series through this backbone, the distances from the real series on fat tails, volatility clustering and the return distribution replace the old distribution-distance row.
metrics.baseline: the same distances between two disjoint stretches of the real series

metrics.why: A deep encoder and decoder joined by skip connections and group normalisation is built to keep gradients flowing through many layers, and the gradient size per epoch shows whether that holds or whether training is exploding or stalling.

The self-attention layer at the bottleneck is the one place where distant positions of the input can inform each other, and the spread of its weights shows whether it looks broadly, fixes on one position or has gone unused.
The host's noise-prediction error per epoch is the only quantity the backbone is trained on, and it shows convergence only; fresh schedule steps and noise in every batch make the curve noisy.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction MSE
notApplicable.why: The network predicts noise and its skip connections bypass the bottleneck, so it rebuilds nothing; its trained error is reported by the held-out denoising error.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: No agreed pretrained feature network for market data exists to define it, and it would describe the host sampler's output, not the backbone.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: The bottleneck is a plain hidden layer with no learned posterior, so no divergence from a prior exists.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: It belongs to contrastive embeddings; the bottleneck here is never read out as an embedding.

notApplicable.name: Held-out log-likelihood
notApplicable.why: The backbone carries the host's equally weighted noise-prediction loss, which is not a bound on the likelihood, so no likelihood belongs to it.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction mean squared error
notApplicable.why: Although the network has an encoder and a decoder, the skip connections let detail bypass the bottleneck and the output is predicted noise, so it is not a compress-and-rebuild model and has no reconstruction error.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet market distance
notApplicable.why: It needs an agreed pretrained feature network that does not exist for market rows, and it would grade the host sampler's output, not the backbone.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler divergence
notApplicable.why: The bottleneck is an ordinary hidden layer with no posterior and no prior, so there is no divergence term.

notApplicable.name: Latent uniformity
notApplicable.why: The bottleneck activations are never used as an embedding and are bypassed by the skip connections, so their spread describes nothing the model is asked to do.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A denoising backbone takes no position; trading results appear only in the as-run layer after Bayes' rule and the engine's trading rule are added.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter never draws a sample, and the image architecture is reduced to one dimension: the bar's current standardised feature row is treated as a one-channel signal along the feature columns, padded to a power-of-two length and given learned position channels, and a one-dimensional U-Net with residual blocks, bottleneck self-attention and skip connections predicts the noise added to it, told whether the bar went up or down. The outcome whose conditioning denoises the whole row better is called likelier through Bayes' rule and one validation-fitted temperature, so the as-run numbers measure a class-conditional model of the current feature row plus that readout, not generated images or paths.
asRun.probabilityNote: For each bar the adapter averages the squared noise-prediction error of the one-dimensional U-Net conditioned on up and conditioned on down over one fixed grid of schedule steps and noise vectors, takes minus those errors as class scores, multiplies them by a single inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows, adds the logarithm of the training class shares and applies a softmax.

stepQuantity.unit: training rows: squared noise-prediction error per feature column; validation rows: nats

meaningful.why: On the test walk this grades the full chain as used: the gap between the U-Net's noise-prediction error under up conditioning and under down conditioning, stretched by the one validation-fitted temperature and shifted by the training class shares; it is unweighted, so it is read against quoting the fold's training up share.

The temperature cannot be negative and the class-share shift is constant, so bars are ordered only by the raw gap between the U-Net's two conditioned errors; this tests whether a convolutional denoiser sliding along the feature columns, whose order carries no meaning, learned anything that separates up rows from down rows.
A bounded check on the same posterior, less ruled than the logarithmic loss by the few bars where a large gap between the U-Net's two errors and the temperature produce near-certain probabilities.

The U-Net's denoising error has no natural probability scale, so honest odds rest on the one temperature fitted on validation rows; this shows whether it still fits on test bars, and without class weighting the comparison with the observed up share is fair.
A slope away from one says the validation temperature stretches the gap between the U-Net's two errors too much or too little on later bars, read without bins.

The position follows the sign of the latest call and a same-direction call is kept with no new trade, so the trade count counts call flips, stops, targets and fold ends.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks label_horizon_bars ahead, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance, never a binomial interval.
For any root other than MNQ the cost charged is the MNQ account figure, a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its own close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.

energy_based_model.summary: A joint energy model (JEM): one network scores every outcome's energy for the row, trained on the labels and, with Langevin-sampled negatives, as a density of the rows themselves.
energy_based_model.implementationNote: Bridge: JEM - f(x) gives the joint energy of (row, outcome); the shared normaliser cancels, so P(k | row) is softmax(f), with one validation temperature. Training: cross-entropy plus the likelihood term with SGLD negatives from a replay buffer; unlabelled training rows count as real data. Differs from the spec: nothing is sampled for use. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.

native.produces: A single energy number for any feature row, low where real rows sit and high elsewhere, from which new rows are drawn by letting noise-driven Langevin steps roll downhill on that energy surface.
native.targetVariable: The unnormalised log density of one row of market features, known only up to a partition constant that cannot be computed.
native.objectiveNote: The specification trains by pushing the energy of real rows down and the energy of rows the model itself sampled with Langevin steps up, because the partition constant that would turn energy into a true likelihood cannot be evaluated.

metrics.why: The energy surface cannot be turned into a likelihood because its partition constant is unknown, so the honest check is to hand a fresh judge the rows the Langevin sampler rolled out of the energy valleys together with real validation rows and see whether it can tell them apart.
metrics.baseline: One half, the hit rate of a judge that cannot separate the sampled rows from the real rows of the same series.

metrics.why: A short Langevin chain can stop on a slope instead of in a valley, so this share shows how many of the sampled rows actually landed inside the neighbourhood where real feature rows of this instrument live.
metrics.baseline: The same share computed for held-out real rows of the same series against the real reference rows.

metrics.why: Langevin chains restarted from a replay buffer tend to keep revisiting the same few deep energy valleys, so this share shows whether the sampled rows reach every kind of real market row or only the most common ones.
metrics.baseline: The same share computed for held-out real rows of the same series against the real reference rows.

metrics.why: An energy network with enough capacity can dig a narrow pit under each training row, and the sampler then simply returns those rows, which this distance ratio exposes while the judge and the neighbourhood shares would still look perfect.
metrics.baseline: One, the ratio obtained when sampled rows sit as far from the training rows as unseen real rows of the same series do.

metrics.why: The logged quantity is the gap between the mean energy of real rows and the mean energy of the sampler's rows, which should hover near balance, and a gap that runs away means the Langevin chains have stopped tracking the energy surface, so it reads as sampler health and never as a score of the model.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: The registry's Wasserstein distance belongs to the stylised-fact table for simulated return paths, and this model samples whole feature rows that are judged by the two-sample judge and the neighbourhood shares instead.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction MSE
notApplicable.why: The energy network turns a row into one number and never rebuilds the row, so a reconstruction error was never defined for this model.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: It depends on a reference embedding network for market rows that does not exist, so the generator stamped a metric that cannot be computed for this model.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: There is no encoder, no latent code and no prior in the energy model the specification describes, so this divergence never applied.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: It measures the spread of contrastive embeddings on a sphere, and an energy model produces an energy surface and sampled rows, never an embedding.

notApplicable.name: Held-out log-likelihood per row
notApplicable.why: The energy is a log density only up to the partition constant, which the specification itself calls intractable, so no likelihood of unseen rows can be stated without a separate estimate that would have to be named.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction mean squared error
notApplicable.why: An energy network maps a row to one number and has no decoder that rebuilds the row, so there is nothing to compare with the input.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler Divergence
notApplicable.why: The energy model described has no encoder and no latent posterior held close to a prior, so there is no divergence term to report.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter is a real joint energy model whose network gives one energy per outcome for the current feature row and is trained with Langevin-sampled negatives from a replay buffer, but nothing it samples is ever used or tested: the Model Cycle reads only the softmax over the two outcome energies as the probability of up, so every as-run number grades the classifier half of the network on the current row and says nothing about the quality of its samples or about future price paths.
asRun.probabilityNote: The network outputs one score per outcome for the standardised feature row, the shared partition constant cancels between the two outcomes, and the probability of up is the softmax of those two scores multiplied by a single inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows, with no class prior added.

stepQuantity.unit: nats for the cross-entropy part, with the weighted energy gap and energy penalty added in energy units

meaningful.why: The classification part of the training loss is an unweighted cross-entropy on the two outcome energies, so on unseen test bars this number grades the same kind of stated odds the network was trained to give, after the single validation temperature has stretched or flattened them.

With two outcomes and no prior term the probability of up is a rising function of the gap between the up energy score and the down energy score, so as long as the fitted inverse temperature stays above zero the ordering of bars is the energy network's own and the size of the temperature does not change it; when validation shows no usable signal the temperature underflows to almost zero, every probability becomes exactly one half and the ordering collapses into pure ties.

It grades the same softmax of the two outcome energies on a bounded scale, so a few bars where the temperature left the network almost certain cannot dominate it the way they dominate the logarithmic loss.

The cross-entropy is not class weighted, so the stated odds are meant to match the up share of the series, and this gap shows whether one temperature fitted on a short validation span was enough to tame the over-confident energy gap.

The only calibration dial this model has is one inverse temperature on the energy gap, and this slope on test bars reads directly whether that dial was set too hot or too cold when it was fitted on the validation rows.

When the validation rows show no usable signal the temperature search drives the inverse temperature to almost zero and every bar is quoted at exactly one half, so this spread of zero shows at once that the collapse happened and that the engine then goes long on every bar of that fold.

The hard call is up whenever the up energy score beats the down energy score, which no temperature above zero can change, so the hit rate tests the energy network's own decision boundary against the fold's majority class; in a fold where the temperature collapsed to almost zero every probability is exactly one half, every bar is called up, and the hit rate only equals the actual up share.

Because the loss is not class weighted the energy gap can lean toward whichever direction was more common in training, and averaging the hit rate of up bars and down bars shows whether the boundary does more than follow that lean.

It sums up in one symmetric number whether the sign of the gap between the two outcome energies moves with the actual direction, with zero meaning the calls carry no more than the training lean; a fold whose temperature collapsed calls every bar up and scores zero here by construction.

It is the money made by going long whenever the up energy score beats the down energy score and short otherwise under the engine's fill rule and costs, read against buy and hold on the same folds; in a fold where the temperature collapsed every probability is exactly one half, the engine goes long on every bar, and this number describes an always-long position rather than the energy network's calls.

It measures how steadily the sign of the energy gap earned money per bar after costs; because only that sign is traded, the size of a fitted temperature above zero does not change it, but a fold whose temperature collapsed to almost zero quotes every bar at exactly one half and is traded always long, so there it measures the steadiness of holding long.

It shows the deepest hole the account fell into while following the energy network's direction call bar after bar, which is the price paid for whatever the calls earned; in a fold where the temperature collapsed it is the drawdown of simply holding long.

It compares what the winning trades opened by a flip in the sign of the energy gap earned with what the losing ones gave back after costs, shown beside the trade count because few flips make it unstable.

It counts how many closed trades ended in profit, where a trade ends when the energy gap changes sign, so it describes the calls under the engine's exit rule and is read together with the predicted up share.

The forecast comes from a second joint energy model fitted separately on quantile bins of the scaled move, whose bin probabilities are blended with each bin's mean training move, so this skill tests that second network against forecasting no change.

It is the size in points of the miss of the second energy model's blended bin means, which can never forecast a move larger than the mean of its outermost training bin and so is read beside the no-change error.
It tests the sign of the second energy model's blended forecast, which is a different network from the one that makes the traded call, so the two direction hit rates need not agree.

A jump in the gradient size before clipping is the first sign that the Langevin negatives have drifted and the energy gap is about to blow up, which the adapter answers by skipping the step and reseeding the replay buffer.

The training curve is the cross-entropy plus the weighted energy gap between real rows and Langevin negatives plus a penalty on squared energies, so its level mixes three things and only its smoothness says whether the sampler stayed stable.
It is the selection score that chose the hidden size and the other dials of the energy network on inner blocks of the training span, optimistic by construction and shown beside the test value.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training curve holds the cross-entropy plus the weighted energy gap and energy penalty while the validation curve holds the plain logarithmic loss of the tempered probability, so their difference compares two different quantities.

With long only switched off and no stop or target the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so the share of bars in the market describes the engine's rule and nothing about the energy network.

The cross-entropy on the outcome energies carries no class weights, so the probability is centred on the training up share and a score that assumes an even prior grades it on a scale it never aimed at.

caveats: The inverse temperature and the kept epoch are both chosen on the same validation rows, and the temperature is refitted at every epoch before that epoch's validation loss is taken, so the validation loss is optimistic and only test bars give a clean reading.
Nothing the Langevin sampler produces is used or scored, so no as-run number speaks to the native question of whether the model's sampled rows look like real rows.

The generative term treats the training span's unlabelled rows, whose horizon move stayed inside the label threshold or crossed a session gap, as extra real data, so the energy surface is shaped by more rows than the classifier is graded on.
A training step whose energy gap explodes or is not finite is skipped and the replay buffer is reseeded from noise, so the logged training curve leaves those steps out.
The price forecast is made by a second, separately fitted energy model over quantile bins of the move and is not the network that makes the traded call.

When validation shows no usable signal in a fold, the fitted inverse temperature collapses to almost zero, every probability of up in that fold is exactly one half, the engine goes long on every bar, the ranking is all ties and the trading numbers of that fold describe an always-long position, so a fold with zero spread in the probability of up must be read that way.
A bar with a missing feature gets no probability and the engine simply keeps the position it already held on that bar.

Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label looks several bars ahead, so any interval around these numbers needs a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.

For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost figure is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption, and the last bar of every fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.

bayesian_generator.summary: Per outcome, a Gaussian mixture with a Dirichlet-process prior over its latent components is fitted by variational Bayes on the whitened rows; the prior decides how many components survive.
bayesian_generator.implementationNote: Bridge: log p(row | outcome) of a variational-Bayes Dirichlet-process Gaussian mixture per outcome on whitened rows, Bayes' rule with training priors, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: its VAE reading is the VAE entry and its Bayesian-weights reading the Bayesian neural hybrid; this is the shallow Bayesian generator. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.

mixture_covariance.label: Covariance
mixture_covariance.description: Full or diagonal covariance per component.

weight_concentration_prior.label: Weight concentration prior
weight_concentration_prior.description: Dirichlet-process concentration: small values keep fewer components.

native.produces: A decoder network that turns a draw from a simple prior over a latent code into a synthetic data row, together with an encoder that gives each real row a distribution over that code and a lower bound on the row's log probability.
native.targetVariable: the joint distribution of the feature columns of one data row, with no statement about the direction of the next move
native.objectiveNote: The specification offers two readings, a variational autoencoder whose bound is taken over a latent code per row and a Bayesian neural network whose bound is taken over the weights, and both trade a reconstruction term against a divergence from a prior.

metrics.why: The encoder and decoder together give only a lower bound on the log probability of an unseen row, so the figure must be labelled as the evidence lower bound or as an importance-weighted bound, and it is the trained objective measured where the decoder could not memorise.
metrics.baseline: the same bound on the fold's own training rows

metrics.why: The row the decoder rebuilds from a sampled code is the first term of the bound, and stating its error as a share of feature variance shows how blurred the Gaussian decoder leaves an unseen bar.
metrics.baseline: rebuilding every row as the training mean of each column

metrics.why: Shows how much of the bound is the price of keeping the encoder's code distribution near the prior; a term near zero means the decoder is ignoring the reparameterised latent code.
Counts the latent dimensions whose encoder mean actually moves from row to row, which is how the collapse that annealing the divergence weight is meant to prevent gets detected.
The bound is the same quantity on training rows and on unseen rows, so a widening gap between the two shows the decoder learning particular training bars instead of their distribution.
When rows are drawn by decoding prior samples for data augmentation, this checks that the drawn rows are new and not near-duplicates of individual training bars.
metrics.baseline: the same distance measured from held-out real rows to their nearest training row

notApplicable.name: Regime Separation Index
notApplicable.why: The latent code is continuous and reparameterised, so there are no discrete regimes whose separation could be measured.

notApplicable.name: fANOVA Variance Explained
notApplicable.why: This describes which search dials mattered in a hyperparameter study and says nothing about the generator's bound or its samples.

notApplicable.name: SHAP Stability Score
notApplicable.why: Attribution stability belongs to a predictor with an output to attribute, and the generator natively predicts nothing about the move.

notApplicable.name: Expected Calibration Error
notApplicable.why: Natively the generator states no probability of up, so there are no stated odds to compare with outcomes; calibration exists only after the Model Cycle adds Bayes' rule on top.

notApplicable.name: Regime Persistence Ratio
notApplicable.why: Each row is encoded on its own with no transition model between rows, so nothing persists from one bar to the next.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: The decoder produces data rows and a bound on their probability, and nothing in the specification makes an up or down call that could be right or wrong.

asRun.standInNote: The specification describes a variational autoencoder or a Bayesian neural network that generates rows; the runnable adapter instead fits one Gaussian mixture with a Dirichlet-process prior to the up rows and one to the down rows of the current feature row, in a whitened principal-direction space, and compares the two densities by Bayes' rule, so every as-run number measures that shallow mixture plus the readout and nothing is generated.
asRun.probabilityNote: The log density of the whitened row under the up mixture and under the down mixture is multiplied by one inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows, the log of each class's training share is added, and a softmax over the two classes gives the probability of up.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per feature column of the negative log density of the whitened row under the mixture of its true outcome on training rows, against nats per scored bar of the logarithmic loss of the probability of up on validation rows, one value for the single fit

meaningful.why: The ordering of bars comes only from the gap between the up mixture's and the down mixture's log density, which the temperature and the prior cannot reorder, so this tests whether the two fitted mixtures really differ where outcomes differ.
Shows what trading the side whose mixture, after the training prior and the temperature, explains the current row better would have earned after costs under the engine's rule.
Grades the posterior from the two mixtures together with the single validation-fitted temperature, so it tests the mixture-plus-temperature pair and not the raw density ratio.
A bounded score of the same Bayes posterior, less dominated than the logarithmic loss by the few bars where one mixture gives the row almost no density.
A slope below one on test bars means the one temperature fitted on validation rows did not tame the over-confident ratio of two full-covariance mixtures.
The prior is the training up share and nothing is class-weighted, so the gap between stated and observed up share tests whether the temperature carried over from validation to test.
A fitted temperature near zero flattens the posterior onto the training prior, and a near-zero spread of the probability of up reveals that the mixtures were judged uninformative.
Counts how often the side favoured by the two mixtures after the prior matched the move; the cut depends on the training up share and the fitted temperature as well as on the densities.
Averages the hit rate on up bars and on down bars, which exposes a posterior that follows the training prior and calls one side almost always.
One symmetric number for whether the mixture-based call moves with the outcome across all four cells, unaffected by a lopsided share of up calls.
Net profit of the mixture-based direction call per unit of bar-to-bar variation, under the engine's holding rule and costs.
The deepest loss run of trading the mixture-based call, which shows how long the two densities stayed on the wrong side.
Winning trade money over losing trade money for the mixture-based call after costs, read beside the trade count because the call flips only when the density gap changes sign.
Share of closed trades of the mixture-based call that ended above zero after costs, which says nothing alone about the size of wins against losses.
Shows whether the posterior from the two mixtures ever leaves the side of the training prior, which decides how to read every trading number.
Tests a second set of mixtures fitted to quantile bins of the scaled move, whose forecast is the posterior-weighted average of the bins' training mean moves, against forecasting no change.
The size in points of the miss of that second, bin-based mixture forecast, which can never reach beyond the mean move of its outermost bin.
How often the sign of the bin-weighted forecast from the second set of mixtures matched the move, on bars where both are non-zero after rounding to the tick.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The fit is a single pass whose training figure is a negative log density per feature column while the validation figure is the logarithmic loss of the probability of up, so their difference compares two different quantities.
Under the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so the share of bars in a position describes the engine's rule and not the mixtures.

caveats: The inverse temperature is fitted on the fold's validation rows, so validation figures are partly in-sample for that one parameter and only the test walk is out of sample.

The whitening projection keeps a fixed number of principal directions computed from all training rows of both classes, so any difference between up and down rows outside those directions is invisible to the mixtures.

The single fit reports one training figure and one validation figure, and the training figure is divided by the full count of feature columns although the density lives in the smaller whitened space, so it is a per-column average of a density over fewer directions and is not the same quantity as the validation figure.
Feature rows are standardised with training statistics and clipped at six standard deviations before the density is evaluated.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.
For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost per side is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.

deep_boltzmann_machine.summary: A two-hidden-layer Gaussian-Bernoulli deep Boltzmann machine whose visible layer holds the row and the outcome; the outcome with the lower free energy is the likely one.
deep_boltzmann_machine.implementationNote: Bridge: joint DBM over (row, one-hot outcome): greedy CD-1 pretraining, then mean-field data statistics and persistent Gibbs chains; score_k is the mean-field lower bound on log p~(row, k), the partition function cancels; validation temperature. Differs from the spec: nothing is sampled for use; the bound is not exact. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.
