native.produces: An unnormalised energy over a data row and two or more layers of hidden binary units, from which synthetic rows are drawn by long runs of alternating Gibbs sampling.
native.targetVariable: the joint distribution of the columns of one data row together with the hidden binary units, with no statement about the direction of the next move
native.objectiveNote: Greedy layer-by-layer contrastive divergence only initialises the weights; the joint phase replaces the data-side expectation with a mean-field fixed point and the model-side expectation with persistent Gibbs chains.

metrics.why: The partition function is intractable, so the direct check is whether a fresh judge can tell rows produced by long Gibbs runs through both hidden layers from real unseen rows.
metrics.baseline: a judge at coin-flip accuracy, which is what indistinguishable rows give

metrics.why: Checks that the rows the Gibbs chains settle on fall inside the neighbourhood of real rows, which fails when the chains are stopped before they have mixed.
The machine is sold on representing many separate kinds of row, and this measures whether the chains visit every kind of real row or stay trapped in a few low-energy wells.
Persistent chains are started from training rows, so this confirms the rows they end on are new and not the starting bars barely altered.
metrics.baseline: the same distance measured from held-out real rows to their nearest training row

metrics.why: Successive Gibbs sweeps are strongly correlated, so the number of independent draws the chains are worth says whether the generated set is large enough to judge at all.

The logged curve is one-step reconstruction error during greedy pretraining and the negative mean-field bound afterwards, so it shows convergence inside each phase and cannot be read across the switch.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: A transport distance between generated and real rows needs a chosen ground metric over dozens of feature columns that the specification never states; the samples are judged by the two-sample judge with precision and recall instead.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction MSE
notApplicable.why: One-step reconstruction is only the monitor of the greedy contrastive-divergence pretraining and can fall while the energy model gets worse, so it does not score the machine.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: No agreed feature extractor for market rows exists in which a Fréchet distance could be computed, and the name was invented by the generator that stamped the table.

notApplicable.name: Latent KL Divergence
notApplicable.why: The hidden units are binary with no prior that an encoder is pulled toward, and the mean-field gap to the true posterior cannot be measured because the true posterior is intractable.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: Uniformity on a sphere grades contrastive embeddings, whereas these hidden layers are binary units and not a normalised embedding.

notApplicable.name: Held-out log-likelihood
notApplicable.why: The normalising constant sums over every visible and hidden configuration and cannot be computed, so any likelihood figure is an annealed-importance-sampling estimate of a bound and must be labelled as one.

notApplicable.name: Reconstruction mean squared error
notApplicable.why: One-step reconstruction is only the monitor of the greedy contrastive-divergence pretraining and can fall while the energy model gets worse, so it does not score the machine.

notApplicable.name: Latent Kullback-Leibler divergence
notApplicable.why: The hidden units are binary with no prior that an encoder is pulled toward, and the mean-field gap to the true posterior cannot be measured because the true posterior is intractable.

asRun.standInNote: The adapter trains a real two-hidden-layer Gaussian-Bernoulli deep Boltzmann machine with greedy contrastive-divergence pretraining, mean-field data statistics and persistent Gibbs chains, but its visible layer holds the current feature row plus a one-hot outcome unit and it is never sampled for use; the as-run numbers measure which outcome unit gives the row the higher mean-field bound, not the quality of generated rows.
asRun.probabilityNote: The mean-field lower bound on the unnormalised log probability of the row is computed once with the up unit switched on and once with the down unit switched on, the partition function cancels in the comparison, and a softmax of the two bounds times one validation-fitted inverse temperature gives the probability of up with no separate prior term.

stepQuantity.unit: squared reconstruction error per column during the pretraining epochs, then nats per row of the negative mean-field bound, against nats per scored bar on validation rows

meaningful.why: The ordering of bars comes only from the gap between the mean-field bound with the up unit on and with the down unit on, which the temperature cannot reorder, so this tests whether the joint machine tied the outcome unit to the row.
Shows what trading the outcome unit that gives the current row the higher mean-field bound would have earned after costs under the engine's rule.
Grades the softmax of the two bounds together with the single validation-fitted temperature; the kept epoch was also chosen on this quantity on validation rows, so only the test value is clean.
A bounded score of the same two-bound posterior, less dominated than the logarithmic loss by bars where the bounds differ by a wide margin.
The two bounds are not equally tight, so a slope away from one on test bars shows the single temperature could not turn their gap into honest odds.
The base rate enters only through the learned bias of the outcome units, so the gap between stated and observed up share tests whether that bias and the temperature hold on test bars.
A fitted temperature near zero flattens the posterior to one half on every bar, and a near-zero spread of the probability of up reveals that the bound gap was judged uninformative.
Counts how often the outcome unit with the higher bound matched the move; with no separate prior term the cut sits wherever the learned outcome biases and the bound gap put it.
Averages the hit rate on up bars and on down bars, which exposes a machine whose outcome bias makes it call one side almost always.
One symmetric number for whether the higher-bound outcome unit moves with the realised direction across all four cells.
Net profit of trading the higher-bound outcome unit per unit of bar-to-bar variation, under the engine's holding rule and costs.
The deepest loss run of trading the higher-bound outcome unit, which shows how long the energy landscape stayed on the wrong side.
Winning trade money over losing trade money for the bound-based call after costs, read beside the trade count because the call flips only when the bound gap changes sign.
Share of closed trades of the bound-based call that ended above zero after costs, which says nothing alone about the size of wins against losses.
Shows whether the bound comparison ever changes side or the learned outcome bias decides every bar, which governs how to read each trading number.

Tests a second Boltzmann machine whose outcome units are quantile bins of the scaled move, with the forecast the posterior-weighted average of the bins' training mean moves, against forecasting no change.
The size in points of the miss of that second, bin-unit machine's forecast, which can never reach beyond the mean move of its outermost bin.
How often the sign of the bin-weighted forecast from the second machine matched the move, on bars where both are non-zero after rounding to the tick.
The update is the clipped difference between mean-field data statistics and persistent-chain statistics, so its size shows whether the chains and the data have stopped disagreeing.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training curve holds reconstruction error and then the negative mean-field bound while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the probability of up, so their difference compares different quantities.
Under the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so the share of bars in a position describes the engine's rule and not the machine.

caveats: The score is a mean-field lower bound and not an exact log probability, and the bound can be tighter for one outcome unit than for the other, which biases their comparison.
The training curve switches quantity when greedy pretraining ends, from one-step reconstruction error to the negative mean-field bound, so it cannot be read as one continuous curve.

The inverse temperature is refitted on the validation rows at every epoch before the validation loss is computed, so the validation curve is in-sample for that one parameter and the kept epoch is chosen on it.
Feature rows are standardised with training statistics and clipped at six standard deviations before the bound is evaluated.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.
For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost per side is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.

masked_autoencoder_density.summary: A class-conditional masked autoencoder hides most of the row's tokens and reconstructs them from the rest; how well each outcome's model fills the gaps ranks the outcomes. MADE masks give an exact likelihood instead.
masked_autoencoder_density.implementationNote: Bridge: score_k is minus the masked Gaussian negative log-likelihood of the hidden tokens (learned per-column variance) averaged over fixed masks, or the exact MADE likelihood with mask_style autoregressive_made; Bayes' rule, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: tokens are groups of feature columns; random masks give a pseudo-likelihood. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths.

native.produces: A reconstruction of the hidden patches of an input from its visible patches, the encoder's latent representation of the visible patches, and in the generative extension new samples made by filling in a fully hidden input step by step.
native.targetVariable: the hidden part of one data row given its visible part, with no statement about the direction of the next move
native.objectiveNote: The squared error is charged only on the hidden patches, never on the visible ones, and the generative variant adds an optional term that pulls the encoder's code toward a prior.

metrics.why: Squared error on the hidden patches of unseen rows is exactly what the encoder and the lightweight decoder are trained on, and scaling it by feature variance shows how much the unmasking improves on filling in the average.
metrics.baseline: filling every hidden column with its training mean

metrics.why: The purpose of hiding patches is a reusable representation, so a probe fitted on the encoder's code of the visible patches is compared with the identical probe fitted on the raw columns and with the same probe on an encoder whose weights were never trained, which separates what masked reconstruction taught from what the architecture and the features already gave.
metrics.baseline: the identical probe fitted on the raw feature columns and on the untrained encoder, scored on the same folds

metrics.why: Detects an encoder whose codes for the visible patches have fallen onto a few directions, which leaves the decoder leaning on its position tokens alone.
The masked error is the same quantity on training rows and unseen rows, so a growing gap shows the decoder learning individual rows, which a high mask ratio is meant to prevent.
Reported only when the optional prior term of the generative variant is switched on, where it shows how strongly the encoder's code is being pulled toward that prior.
Applies when rows are produced by iterative unmasking from a fully hidden input and confirms the filled-in rows are not replays of training bars.
metrics.baseline: the same distance measured from held-out real rows to their nearest training row

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: A transport distance between drawn and real rows would test the slow iterative sampler under a ground metric the specification never chooses, while the model is trained and judged on filling hidden patches.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: No agreed feature extractor for market rows exists in which a Fréchet distance could be computed, and the name was invented by the generator that stamped the table.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: Uniformity on the unit sphere belongs to contrastive encoders with normalised outputs; this reconstruction-trained encoder is checked for collapse by the effective rank of its code instead.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: Natively the autoencoder fills in hidden patches and makes no up or down call; a direction appears only when the Model Cycle compares two class-conditioned copies.

notApplicable.name: Held-out log-likelihood
notApplicable.why: The plain masked autoencoder is trained on squared error over hidden patches and assigns no probability to a row; only the generative extension with a prior and iterative unmasking could, and then only as a pseudo-likelihood averaged over random masks that would have to be labelled as such.

asRun.standInNote: The adapter trains a real transformer masked autoencoder, but its tokens are small groups of feature columns of the current row instead of image patches, it is conditioned on the outcome, and it is scored by how well each outcome's copy fills the hidden groups; the as-run numbers measure that fill-in comparison plus Bayes' rule, not a representation and not generated rows.
asRun.probabilityNote: For each outcome the Gaussian negative log-likelihood of the hidden column groups given the visible ones is averaged over a fixed set of masks, its negative is multiplied by one inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows, the log of each class's training share is added, and a softmax over the two outcomes gives the probability of up.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per feature column of the masked Gaussian negative log-likelihood on training rows, against nats per scored bar on validation rows

meaningful.why: The ordering of bars comes only from how much better the up-conditioned copy fills the hidden column groups than the down-conditioned copy, which the temperature and the prior cannot reorder, so this tests the fill-in comparison itself.
Shows what trading the outcome whose conditioned autoencoder, after the training prior and the temperature, fills in the current row better would have earned after costs under the engine's rule.
Grades the posterior built from the two fill-in scores together with the single validation-fitted temperature, so it tests the pair and not the raw pseudo-likelihood gap.
A bounded score of the same posterior, less dominated than the logarithmic loss by bars where one outcome's copy reconstructs the hidden groups far worse.
A gap between two pseudo-likelihoods has no natural probability scale, so a slope away from one on test bars shows the single temperature did not supply one.
The prior is the training up share and nothing is class-weighted, so the gap between stated and observed up share tests whether the temperature carried over from validation to test.
A fitted temperature near zero flattens the posterior onto the training prior, and a near-zero spread of the probability of up reveals that the fill-in gap was judged uninformative.

Counts how often the outcome favoured by the fill-in comparison after the prior matched the move; the cut depends on the training up share and the fitted temperature as well as on the reconstructions.
Averages the hit rate on up bars and on down bars, which exposes a posterior that follows the training prior and calls one side almost always.
One symmetric number for whether the better-filling outcome moves with the realised direction across all four cells.
Net profit of the fill-in-based direction call per unit of bar-to-bar variation, under the engine's holding rule and costs.
The deepest loss run of trading the fill-in-based call, which shows how long the two conditioned copies stayed on the wrong side.
Winning trade money over losing trade money for the fill-in-based call after costs, read beside the trade count because the call flips only when the score gap changes sign.
Share of closed trades of the fill-in-based call that ended above zero after costs, which says nothing alone about the size of wins against losses.
Shows whether the fill-in comparison ever leaves the side of the training prior, which decides how to read every trading number.
Tests a second masked autoencoder conditioned on quantile bins of the scaled move, whose forecast is the posterior-weighted average of the bins' training mean moves, against forecasting no change.
The size in points of the miss of that second, bin-conditioned autoencoder's forecast, which can never reach beyond the mean move of its outermost bin.
How often the sign of the bin-weighted forecast from the second autoencoder matched the move, on bars where both are non-zero after rounding to the tick.
The size of the update to the encoder and decoder under freshly drawn random masks, which shows whether the masked fit has settled or is still being pushed around by the masks.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training curve holds the masked Gaussian negative log-likelihood per feature column while the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the probability of up, so their difference compares different quantities.
Under the default dials the engine is always long or short once the first call is made, so the share of bars in a position describes the engine's rule and not the autoencoder.

caveats: With the default random masks the score is a pseudo-likelihood averaged over a fixed set of masks and not a normalised density, so the softmax is not an exact Bayes posterior; only the autoregressive mask style gives an exact likelihood.

The kept epoch is the one with the lowest validation negative score of the true class per feature column, not the lowest validation logarithmic loss that the chart plots, so the marked best epoch need not be the low point of the plotted validation curve; the registry's checkpoint field has no value for this criterion, so it reads none here although an epoch is selected.
The inverse temperature is refitted on the validation rows at every epoch before the validation loss is computed, so the validation curve is in-sample for that one parameter.

Feature rows are standardised with training statistics and clipped at six standard deviations before scoring, and the grouping of feature columns into tokens follows column order, which carries no meaning.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so intervals need a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next open.
For roots other than the micro Nasdaq contract the cost per side is that contract's account figure applied as a stated assumption.

variational_autoencoder_density.summary: A class-conditional VAE compresses the row into a latent code under each outcome; the importance-weighted bound on its likelihood feeds Bayes' rule.
variational_autoencoder_density.implementationNote: Bridge: log p(row | outcome) by the importance-weighted bound (one fixed noise tensor) of a class-conditional Gaussian VAE trained on the ELBO; Bayes' rule with training priors, validation temperature. Differs from the spec: the latent code is not used on its own and nothing is generated. Expect: Class-conditional density of the current feature row plus Bayes' rule; not a model of future paths. Bound looseness can differ by outcome.

native.produces: For each input row the encoder outputs the mean and spread of a Gaussian latent code, the decoder rebuilds the row from a draw of that code, and together they give a lower bound on the log probability of the row plus the ability to draw new rows by decoding samples from the standard normal prior.
native.targetVariable: The probability density of an observed data row, stated as a lower bound on its log probability, together with the compressed latent code of that row.
native.objectiveNote: The variational autoencoder's version adds the reparameterised latent draw (mean plus spread times standard normal noise), which lets the reconstruction term and the Kullback-Leibler divergence to the standard normal prior be minimised together by ordinary gradient descent.

metrics.why: The encoder and decoder are trained to raise a lower bound on the log probability of each row, so the same bound on rows the network never trained on is the model's own score, and the record must say that the figure is a bound and which bound it is rather than an exact likelihood.
metrics.baseline: The same bound from the same network with its decoder ignoring the latent code, which is a single Gaussian per feature column fitted on the training rows.

metrics.why: The decoder rebuilds each row from a noisy draw of the latent code, so the share of feature variance lost on unseen rows shows how much of the row survives the squeeze through the latent neck, which is the first of the two terms the training loss trades off.
metrics.baseline: The error of rebuilding every unseen row as the training mean of each feature column, which loses all of the feature variance.

metrics.why: The second term of the training loss charges the encoder for moving its Gaussian code away from the standard normal prior, and reading it apart from the reconstruction term shows whether the bound is being earned by using the code or by ignoring it.
The divergence charge can grow until the decoder stops reading the latent code, and counting the latent units whose encoder mean still moves from row to row is the direct check for that collapse.
metrics.baseline: The configured latent size of the same network.

metrics.why: Natively the same negative lower bound is computed on training rows and on validation rows, so a validation value well above the training value means the encoder and decoder have memorised the training rows instead of learning where rows in general fall.

The specification's generative use is decoding draws from the standard normal prior into new rows, and this ratio shows whether those decoded rows are fresh or are near copies of rows the decoder was trained to rebuild.
metrics.baseline: The same nearest-training-row distance measured for real rows held out of training.

metrics.why: The decoder can turn draws from the standard normal prior into new rows, and the share of those decoded rows that land inside the neighbourhood of real held-out rows shows whether the draws look like market feature rows at all, which the copying ratio alone cannot show because a decoder that outputs one blurred average row is far from every training row and still passes it.
metrics.baseline: The same neighbourhood share measured for real held-out rows against the training rows.

metrics.why: Real held-out rows are only reproduced if the decoded prior draws spread over every kind of row the training rows contain, so the share of real rows that fall inside the neighbourhood of the decoded rows exposes a decoder that covers one mode of the feature rows and ignores the rest.
metrics.baseline: The same coverage share measured for a second set of real held-out rows in place of the decoded rows.

notApplicable.name: Wasserstein Distance
notApplicable.why: The model's native score is its own lower bound on the log probability of unseen rows, and a transport distance between sampled and real return distributions belongs to path simulators rather than to a density of the feature row.

notApplicable.name: Fréchet Market Distance
notApplicable.why: No reference embedding network for market rows exists to compute a Fréchet distance in, and the stamped table invented the metric without a definition the engine or the registry could follow.

notApplicable.name: Latent Uniformity
notApplicable.why: Uniformity is a target for contrastive embeddings on a sphere, while this latent code is regularised toward a standard normal prior and checked by the count of active latent units instead.

notApplicable.name: Accuracy
notApplicable.why: Natively the encoder and decoder never see an outcome label and predict no direction, so a hit rate exists only after a runnable bridge adds a readout that reads labels.

notApplicable.name: Sharpe ratio
notApplicable.why: A density model of a data row takes no position, so a return per unit of risk describes the Model Cycle's trading rule applied to the bridge's call and not the variational autoencoder itself.

asRun.standInNote: The runnable adapter trains one class-conditional Gaussian variational autoencoder on the current standardised feature row, with the outcome fed to the encoder and decoder through a learned class embedding, then scores each row under the up class and under the down class with an importance-weighted bound and turns the two bounds into a probability of up by Bayes' rule with training priors and one inverse temperature fitted on validation rows; the latent code is never used on its own and nothing is generated, so every as-run number measures this density-ratio classifier of the present row and not a generator of future paths.
asRun.probabilityNote: For each bar the frozen network computes an importance-weighted bound on the log density of the standardised feature row under the up class and under the down class from one fixed tensor of latent noise, multiplies the two bounds by a single inverse temperature found by golden-section search on the validation rows, adds the log of the smoothed training class counts and takes the softmax share of the up class.

stepQuantity.unit: nats per feature column for the training curve and nats per scored validation bar for the validation curve

meaningful.why: The ordering of bars comes only from the gap between the importance-weighted bound under the up class and the bound under the down class, and a positive inverse temperature cannot reorder it, so this number tests the density ratio itself with no help from the validation-fitted scale.

The fit uses no class weights and the priors are the training class counts, so the stated odds aim at the real base rate and this proper score grades the density ratio together with its one validation-fitted inverse temperature against quoting the fold's training up share on every bar.

It grades the same Bayes posterior on a bounded scale, so a few bars where the two class bounds disagree violently and the posterior lands near certainty cannot dominate the score the way they can in the logarithmic loss.

A density ratio over many feature columns is over-confident before scaling, and this slope on test bars shows whether the single inverse temperature fitted on the validation rows still puts the posterior on the right scale later in the fold.

Because the posterior uses training class counts as priors and no class weighting, comparing stated odds with observed up shares is a fair check of the bridge, read with the occupied-bin count since a small temperature packs every bar near the prior.

When the validation rows give the density ratio no support the fitted inverse temperature falls toward zero and every bar receives the training prior, and a spread near zero here is how that collapse shows on the scoreboard.

With the temperature near zero the posterior equals the training prior on every bar and the call becomes the training majority class throughout the fold, so the called-up share must be read before any hit rate or trading number.

The hard call asks whether the up-class bound times the temperature plus the log prior beats the down-class side, so the hit rate tests the sign of the density ratio shifted by the training prior and is read against the majority-class accuracy of the same fold.
Averaging the recall of up bars and of down bars shows whether the two class-conditional densities separate both outcomes or whether the training prior alone is deciding the call.

It condenses the four confusion cells into one symmetric correlation, and it comes back undefined, not zero, when the Bayes posterior collapses to the training prior and the model calls one direction on every bar, so an empty value here is itself the sign of that collapse.

The engine goes long when the Bayes posterior of up is at least one half and short otherwise, so this is what the sign of the prior-shifted density ratio earned after costs, read beside buy and hold on the same folds.

It states the per-bar net result of trading the density-ratio call per unit of its own variability, and it is also the quantity the hyperparameter search maximised on inner training blocks when it chose the latent size, hidden size and learning rate.
It shows the deepest hole dug while the position followed the sign of the class-conditional density comparison, which matters because the generative fit never saw a trading loss during training.
It compares the money won and lost on trades opened and closed by flips of the Bayes call, after costs, and so depends on how often the two class bounds swap order from bar to bar.

It counts the share of closed trades that ended positive under the engine's flip-or-hold rule applied to the density-ratio call, and is read with the trade count because a call that rarely flips closes few trades.

The forecast comes from a second, separately fitted variational autoencoder conditioned on quantile bins of the scaled move, whose Bayes posterior over the bins weights each bin's mean training move, and this number tests that readout against forecasting no change.

It gives the miss of the posterior-weighted bin mean in points, read beside the no-change error on the same bars because a forecast built from a handful of bin means cannot reach outside the training bins' range.
It tests the sign of the bin-weighted forecast from the second density model, which is fitted apart from the two-class direction model and can therefore disagree with the traded call.

measuredNotMeaningful.why: The training curve holds the negative evidence lower bound per feature column and the validation curve holds the logarithmic loss of the probability of up, so their difference compares two different quantities.
With the long-only switch off and no stop or target set the engine is never flat once the first call is filled, so the exposure share describes the engine's rule and not the density model.

caveats: The kept epoch is the one with the lowest validation negative importance-weighted bound of the true class per feature column, which is not the logarithmic loss of the probability of up: that loss is plotted for every epoch but did not choose the epoch, so the recorded selection value none means that none of the listed selection quantities applies, and the test logarithmic loss is not a selected-on number.
The second density model behind the price forecast keeps its epoch the same way, on the negative bound of the true price bin and not on the forecast error.
The inverse temperature is fitted on the fold's validation rows, so the validation loss curve is partly in sample for that one parameter and only the test walk is out of sample.
The importance-weighted bound can be looser for one outcome than for the other, which shifts the density ratio in a way the single temperature and the training priors cannot correct.

A divergence weight other than one means the training loss is no longer a true lower bound, although the importance-weighted score used for the posterior remains a valid bound for any encoder and decoder.
Consecutive scored bars share future bars because the label horizon overlaps, so any interval around these numbers must use a block bootstrap or a Newey-West variance and never a binomial interval.
For roots other than the Micro Nasdaq contract the cost figures are the Micro Nasdaq account figures applied as a stated assumption.
The last bar of each fold exits at its close while every other exit fills at the next bar's open.
